title: Structural insights into subtype-specific agonist recognition by sphingosine-1-phosphate receptors
experiments_summary:
1. BRET-based Gi1 dissociation assays: A bioluminescence resonance energy transfer (BRET) assay was used to evaluate the activation profiles of four agonists (CYM5442, HY-X-1011, Ponesimod, SAR247799) and S1P across S1PR1-S1PR5. HEK293T cells were co-transfected with receptor, Gαi1-Rluc8, Gβ1, and Gγ2-GFP2 constructs in a 1:1:1:1 ratio; coelenterazine 400a was used as the substrate; BRET ratios were measured at 395 nm and 510 nm emission. This assay was also applied to WT and alanine-scanning/reciprocal mutants of S1PR1, S1PR3, and S1PR5 to assess effects on receptor activation potency and efficacy.

2. Cryo-EM structure determination: Four S1PR1-Gi1 complexes bound to CYM5442, HY-X-1011, Ponesimod, or SAR247799 were assembled using established protocols. S1PR1 (with N-terminal BRIL fusion) was co-expressed with Gαi1 and Gβ1γ2 in Sf9 insect cells. Complexes were purified via sequential anti-Flag affinity chromatography, Ni-NTA chromatography, incubation with scFv16, and size-exclusion chromatography. ScFv16 was separately expressed in Hi5 cells and purified by Ni-Sepharose chromatography. Cryo-EM grids were prepared using Vitrobot Mark IV, and data were collected on a 300 kV Titan Krios Gi3 with a Gatan K3 detector. Data processing used cryoSPARC (for three complexes) and RELION 5.0/cryoSPARC/CryoSIEVE (for SAR247799 complex), yielding maps at 3.69, 2.79, 2.79, and 2.97 Å resolution. Structural models were built in COOT, refined in Phenix, and validated using MolProbity.

3. Alanine scanning mutagenesis combined with BRET assays: Selected residues in the ligand-binding pocket of S1PR1 were individually mutated to alanine, and reciprocal mutations were introduced between S1PR1/S1PR3 and S1PR1/S1PR5 residue pairs (e.g., L276F/F263L at position 6.55, L297I/I284L at position 7.39, S129G/G123S at 3.37, T207I/I201T at 5.44, V132T/T126V at 3.40, and triple mutants at positions 3.41, 5.46, 5.50). The effect of R78A (position 2.37) at the Gi-binding interface was also assessed. All mutants were cloned into pcDNA3.1, expressed in HEK293T cells, and tested in the BRET Gi1 dissociation assay.

4. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and TAPS path optimization: Agonists were docked into inactive (S1PR1 PDB: 3V2Y; S1PR3 and S1PR5 homology-modeled from 3V2Y) and active structures (S1PR1 PDB: 7VIE; S1PR3 PDB: 7EW3; S1PR5 PDB: 7EW1) using AutoDock 4.2. Systems were prepared with CHARMM-GUI Membrane Builder (POPC bilayer, TIP3P water, 0.15 M NaCl, CHARMM36 force field). Standard MD equilibration and 100 ns production runs were performed in GROMACS-2019.4. Targeted MD (tMD) simulations were carried out using GROMACS and PLUMED to generate initial transition paths from inactive to active states. The TAPS method was then applied to optimize minimum free energy paths (MFEPs). Convergence was evaluated by multidimensional scaling and PCV-z analysis. Umbrella sampling with WHAM was used to compute free energy profiles along the MFEPs, quantifying activation barriers (ΔGT) and intermediate state stabilities (ΔGI) for each ligand-receptor combination. Distance measurements between agonist tail ends and residue 5.50 were extracted from TAPS trajectories to assess pocket penetration depth.
